# Waters of Bahia Inglesa, Chile

April 16, 2018[SouthAmerica](https://www.southamericatotheworld.com/author/southamerica/ "SouthAmerica")

For much of length of the very long Peru and Chile coastline, the beach sands are dark gray, mirroring their andesite source terrane from which much of the sediment was derived. Bahia Inglesa overcomes this norm by having more whitish sand from addition of shell material. The waters along the Chilean coastline are frigid, and yet full of nutrients, supports a large fishery, and lively coastal communities of shellfish fauna. The Bahia Inglesa sand really has two components, the white shell material, and darker grains, giving it a salt and pepper appearance. The sand color is important for imparting to the shallow water in coves between craggy rocks a light blue hue. The water’s color is enough to convince somebody for a pleasant time in the Pacific, until you feel the temperature!

[![Image 3: southamericatotheworld.com](https://i0.wp.com/www.southamericatotheworld.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/04/Bahia-de-Inglesa-sand-1.jpg?resize=300%2C200&ssl=1)](https://i0.wp.com/www.southamericatotheworld.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/04/Bahia-de-Inglesa-sand-1.jpg?ssl=1)

Close up photograph of sand from Bahia Inglesa. About 80 percent of the grains are from shell fragments, thereby explaining the overall whiter character of the beach.

Bahia Inglesa is located off of the Panamericana Highway at the general latitude of Copiapό, and is just south of the small fishing port called [**Caldera**](https://www.southamericatotheworld.com/south-america-food-blog-living-peru-chile-argentina-yanira-k-wise-james-m-wise/granito-orbicular-of-chile/). The quickest approach is the flight to Copiapό, which lands closer to this beach than to the town, at the [**Atacama**](https://www.southamericatotheworld.com/south-america-food-blog-living-peru-chile-argentina-yanira-k-wise-james-m-wise/flowers-in-the-worlds-driest-desert/) airport. At both Caldera and Bahia Inglesa the small town sites offer restaurants having fresh catch of the day, where the Dorado and Corvina (sea bass) are recommended. Caldera has more services while the village at Bahia Inglesa exists for servicing tourists that flock here in the summer months to enjoy the aforementioned white sands.

[![Image 4: southamericatotheworld.com](https://i0.wp.com/www.southamericatotheworld.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/04/Bahia-Inglesa-Chile-1.jpg?resize=300%2C225&ssl=1)](https://i0.wp.com/www.southamericatotheworld.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/04/Bahia-Inglesa-Chile-1.jpg?ssl=1)

Town of Bahia Inglesa

About 16 km to the south is another series of less developed beaches at Bahia de Chorrillos that are also worth checking out.

Caldera Museum- the relatively low coastal plains behind Bahia Inglesa feature Pliocene marine deposits that include whale fossils. Old sea cliffs cut into this material is distinct on the aerial photographs. A similar shallow marine basin that is now uplifted exposing whale fossils in Peru surrounds the port town of Pisco, however, Bahia Inglesa wins for having the stunning water colors and whiter sand. Any Chile road trip exploring the length of the country should place a stop at this tranquil beach.

[![Image 5: southamericatotheworld.com](https://i0.wp.com/www.southamericatotheworld.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/04/Bahia-Inglesa-Chile-2.jpg?resize=300%2C225&ssl=1)](https://i0.wp.com/www.southamericatotheworld.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/04/Bahia-Inglesa-Chile-2.jpg?ssl=1)

Bahia Inglesa

We have seen many of the beaches along the Chilean coastline, and can say that Bahia Inglesa is one of the nicer sections to visit.

# Caldera, Chile: Taking in the Quiet Fishing Village and Jewel-Colored Bahía Inglesa

[![Image 2: Views from Caldera, Chile](https://farm1.staticflickr.com/701/21258185509_5d9ab1768b_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/21258185509/in/dateposted-public/ "Views from Caldera, Chile")  
_Pelicans and Other Seabirds in Caldera, Chile_

There’s no way around it: northern Chile is vast. Chile is a long, skinny country with miles upon endless miles of coastline, dotted here and there with important port cities or crossroads towns connecting to an inland highway. When heading north from Santiago by land, you may ask yourself one of two questions: can I endure spending 24+ hours on a bus? or, where can I stop?

[![Image 3: Views from Caldera, Chile](https://farm6.staticflickr.com/5633/21434277652_2f1856a100_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/21434277652/in/dateposted-public/ "Views from Caldera, Chile")  
_Quiet Little Beach and Houses Overlooking the Bay of Caldera, Chile_

While I spent 32 hours on a bus [once before](https://www.blueskylimit.com/blog/2013/08/11/six-weeks-on-the-road-in-chile-and-argentina/), I vowed never to do that again. When I decided to visit Iquique for the second half of my winter vacation, I knew I wanted to break the journey somewhere along the way.

[![Image 4: Views from Caldera, Chile](https://farm1.staticflickr.com/614/21434963252_7df95b4d63_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/21434963252/in/dateposted-public/ "Views from Caldera, Chile")  
_Plaza de Armas in Caldera, Chile_

Enter Caldera. Caldera is about 12 hours north of Santiago and 12 hours south of Iquique and located right off the Panamerican highway, making it an easily accessible and convenient stop on a bus journey along the coast. After hearing rave reviews of the town from two of my volunteers, I decided to see it for myself.

[![Image 5: Views from Caldera, Chile](https://farm1.staticflickr.com/564/21433798112_093d394658_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/21433798112/in/dateposted-public/ "Views from Caldera, Chile")  
_Fishing Boats Docked in Caldera, Chile_

Caldera is a town known for its artisanal fishing methods, for being the site of the [first railroad](http://www.memoriachilena.cl/602/w3-article-3401.html) in Chile, for its colonial arquitecture, and for its pleasant beaches. By coincidence, I decided to visit Caldera on the weekend it was celebrating the anniversary of the first railroad, which gave the usually quiet town lots of fun energy and life.

[![Image 6: Views from Caldera, Chile](https://farm6.staticflickr.com/5736/20824291183_0eba350477_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/20824291183/in/dateposted-public/ "Views from Caldera, Chile")  
_Relaxing at the Beach in Caldera, Chile_

To be fair, there isn’t much to do in Caldera except relax. I spent some time sitting by the ocean, looking out at the fishing boats docked in the bay. I took in the colorful plaza, which on one side is your typical Plaza de Armas, and on the other is a mini amusement park. I wandered the streets looking at the colonial buildings. And of course, I ate [artesanal ice cream](https://instagram.com/p/5S0hwauLAf/) from a local shop.

[![Image 7: Views from Caldera, Chile](https://farm6.staticflickr.com/5777/20822515894_e99278b4bf_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/20822515894/in/dateposted-public/ "Views from Caldera, Chile")  
_Converted Train Cars Sell Souvenirs in Caldera, Chile_

I poked around the old railroad station, which is now a Centro Cultural. Because of the anniversary weekend, there were a lot of food stands selling regional treats like my much-loved _churrasca_.

[![Image 8: Churrasca in Caldera, Chile](https://farm6.staticflickr.com/5700/21453207851_46730f03f2_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/21453207851/in/dateposted-public/ "Churrasca in Caldera, Chile")  
_Can’t Resist a Churrasca in Caldera, Chile_

[![Image 9: Views from Caldera, Chile](https://farm6.staticflickr.com/5821/21434206142_d0d870c784_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/21434206142/in/dateposted-public/ "Views from Caldera, Chile")  
_Old Caldera Railway Sign_

After getting a sense of the town, I wandered over to the fishing docks and watched the pelicans, my favorite seabird. I also watched the sea lions lumbering around on the rocks, going about their business.

[![Image 10: Views from Caldera, Chile](https://farm6.staticflickr.com/5808/21434030362_dc15f20e17_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/21434030362/in/dateposted-public/ "Views from Caldera, Chile")  
_Watching the Seabirds Along the Coastal Desert in Caldera, Chile_

[![Image 11: Views from Caldera, Chile](https://farm1.staticflickr.com/717/21257134088_0ff62db9fe_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/21257134088/in/dateposted-public/ "Views from Caldera, Chile")  
_Sea Lion Doing His Thing in Caldera, Chile_

As a vegetarian, I wasn’t tempted by the seafood restaurants or museum on fishing methods, but I did appreciate the murals celebrating traditional fisherman, who also form part of my own family tree, many generations back.

[![Image 12: Views from Caldera, Chile](https://farm1.staticflickr.com/767/21256995268_ef3e5c37c3_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/21256995268/in/dateposted-public/ "Views from Caldera, Chile")  
_Mural of a Traditional Fisherman, Caldera, Chile_

The next morning, the hostal lent me a bike and I headed back into town to watch the main ceremony recreating the first departure of Chile’s first railroad.

[![Image 13: Anniversary of the First Railroad in Chile, Caldera, Chile](https://farm6.staticflickr.com/5648/21444477965_8f042a8369_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/21444477965/in/dateposted-public/ "Anniversary of the First Railroad in Chile, Caldera, Chile")  
_Caldera Residents Dressed in Period Costumes_

I appreciated that so many of Caldera’s residents went all out in wearing traditional clothing from the 1800’s. It was nice to see a celebration that was not religious, but rather historical, in nature. After welcoming trekkers who hiked overnight to arrive in Caldera, it was time to cut the ribbon and board the train.

[![Image 14: Anniversary of the First Railroad in Chile, Caldera, Chile](https://farm6.staticflickr.com/5692/21452883871_f3080a0dfe_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/21452883871/in/dateposted-public/ "Anniversary of the First Railroad in Chile, Caldera, Chile")

[![Image 15: Anniversary of the First Railroad in Chile, Caldera, Chile](https://farm6.staticflickr.com/5710/20821672584_c5881b9516_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/20821672584/in/dateposted-public/ "Anniversary of the First Railroad in Chile, Caldera, Chile")  
_Time to Get on the Train in Caldera, Chile_

From the center of town, I biked over to the other major destination in Caldera, the Gruta del Padre Negro, a small church sanctuary honoring a priest from Colombia who is known for granting miracles.

[![Image 16: Gruta del Padre Negro, Caldera, Chile](https://farm6.staticflickr.com/5823/20821631744_5318ef9f5a_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/20821631744/in/dateposted-public/ "Gruta del Padre Negro, Caldera, Chile")  
_Gruta del Padre Negro, Caldera, Chile_

The small building has colorful murals painted all over its interior and the inviting plaza is also a good place to break for a snack.

[![Image 17: Gruta del Padre Negro, Caldera, Chile](https://farm1.staticflickr.com/681/21256471728_8ec6af155b_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/21256471728/in/dateposted-public/ "Gruta del Padre Negro, Caldera, Chile")

[![Image 18: Gruta del Padre Negro, Caldera, Chile](https://farm1.staticflickr.com/588/20823187353_724f949d78_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/20823187353/in/dateposted-public/ "Gruta del Padre Negro, Caldera, Chile")  
_Murals in the Gruta del Padre Negro, Caldera, Chile_

[![Image 19: Gruta del Padre Negro, Caldera, Chile](https://farm1.staticflickr.com/753/21452737151_36a855e517_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/21452737151/in/dateposted-public/ "Gruta del Padre Negro, Caldera, Chile")  
_Lighting Candles for Miracles in the Gruta del Padre Negro, Caldera, Chile_

I continued along my way the 6km bike path to Bahía Inglesa, a popular tourist destination due to its white sand beaches and jewel-toned waters.

[![Image 20: Views from Bahía Inglesa, Caldera, Chile](https://farm1.staticflickr.com/580/20821433594_2fd1e132fb_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/20821433594/in/dateposted-public/ "Views from Bahía Inglesa, Caldera, Chile")  
_White Sand Beaches and Jewel-Toned Waters in Bahía Inglesa, Caldera, Chile_

[![Image 21: Views from Bahía Inglesa, Caldera, Chile](https://farm1.staticflickr.com/672/21255858840_a3ae4810e9_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/21255858840/in/dateposted-public/ "Views from Bahía Inglesa, Caldera, Chile")  
_Bahía Inglesa, Caldera, Chile_

Bahía Inglesa is even smaller than Caldera, consisting mainly of beachfront restaurants and cabañas for rent during the tourist season. Although I had planned to spend a leisurely afternoon reading on the beach, the winter winds coming off the water were quite chilly so I decided to head back to Caldera.

[![Image 22: Views from Bahía Inglesa, Caldera, Chile](https://farm1.staticflickr.com/782/21255836490_daea3b6b8d_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/21255836490/in/dateposted-public/ "Views from Bahía Inglesa, Caldera, Chile")  
_Selfie with a Photobomb by a Street Dog, Bahía Inglesa, Caldera, Chile_

On the way, I stopped at a viewpoint overlooking Bahía Inglesa, where I took in the surrounding landscape. It surprises me how similar coastal Chile is to coastal Peru, considering the distance, with barren deserts inland and lovely beaches and bays on the water.

[![Image 23: Views from Viewpoint near Bahía Inglesa, Caldera, Chile](https://farm1.staticflickr.com/563/21255746640_9ff4bb4e20_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/21255746640/in/dateposted-public/ "Views from Viewpoint near Bahía Inglesa, Caldera, Chile")  
_Looking Over Bahía Inglesa, Caldera, Chile_

[![Image 24: Views from Viewpoint near Bahía Inglesa, Caldera, Chile](https://farm1.staticflickr.com/573/21255767860_98b12ee210_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/21255767860/in/dateposted-public/ "Views from Viewpoint near Bahía Inglesa, Caldera, Chile")  
_Empty Desert Landscape Near Bahiá Inglesa, Caldera, Chile_

After returning to Caldera, I took another spin around the town. One thing I thought I would love about Caldera is that it hosts a moai from [Easter Island](https://www.blueskylimit.com/blog/category/chile/easter-island-rapa-nui/).

[![Image 25: Moai from Easter Island in Caldera, Chile](https://farm1.staticflickr.com/631/21489411816_d253e163c9_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/21489411816/in/dateposted-public/ "Moai from Easter Island in Caldera, Chile")  
_Moai from Easter Island in Caldera, Chile_

Easter Island is located at about the same latitude as Caldera, so the moai was donated to mark this relationship.

[![Image 26: Moai from Easter Island in Caldera, Chile](https://farm6.staticflickr.com/5723/20894485073_acff23c645_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/20894485073/in/dateposted-public/ "Moai from Easter Island in Caldera, Chile")  
_Moai from Easter Island, Looking Out to the Sea in Caldera, Chile_

Unfortunately, as with many moai on mainland Chile, this moai has been treated poorly by visitors and is sadly covered with disgusting graffiti.

[![Image 27: Moai in Caldera, Chile](https://farm1.staticflickr.com/587/21256488880_bba181c8b6_n.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/21256488880/in/dateposted-public/ "Moai in Caldera, Chile")  
_Much-Abused But Still Dignified Moai in Caldera, Chile_

As the sun went down, I headed back to my _hostal_ to wait out the remaining hours until my bus to Iquique, where I would spend the remainder of my winter vacation, enjoying the warmer temperatures of the north!

**Recommendations for Caldera, Chile:**

*   Caldera would be a perfect weekend trip and seemed to be a big destination for vacationing couples and families. If I had been in the mood to relax on a retreat, I would have enjoyed staying for longer, but I was antsy to move on to the big city.
*   I stayed at [Hostal El Faro](http://www.casahostalelfaro.com/), which is owned by an extremely sweet woman named Mariela. You can book the hostel through AirBnB or on her [website](http://www.casahostalelfaro.com/). Mariela is incredibly helpful and will pick you up from the bus terminal if you arrange in advance, give you a brief tour of the town to get you situated, and provide suggestions for your visit. She also went out of her way and drove me to the bus station at midnight, and her son lent me a bike for my trip to Bahía Inglesa. I highly recommend staying here as long as you don’t mind being a little ways out of the downtown area. I like walking and it was certainly walkable, but I do suggest using Google Maps to find your way!
*   The Gruta del Padre Negro is located on the outskirts of town and is worth a stop to see some of the religious heritage of the town.
*   As mentioned, I happened to visit when the town was celebrating the anniversary of the first railroad in Chile. I appreciated the period costumes and celebrations for the anniversary of the railroad, and if you’re interested in seeing it for yourself, plan a visit in July. More info [here](http://www.ellapicero.cl/caldera-esta-de-fiesta-por-aniversario-de-primer-ferrocarril/) on the festivities in 2015.
*   Bahia Inglesa is an easy 6km trip on paved bike paths from Caldera, as long as you have a good bike. There are bike rental shops in town, or your hostal may be able to lend you one.
*   There is an artisanal ice cream shop in town, popular among tourists, called Helados Gutierrez.
*   Pullman and Turbus stop at the tiny bus terminal in town, but you want to make sure you book your ticket in advance and store your luggage at your hostal as the offices are not open at all hours.
*   Other sights to see in town are the Centro Cultural Ferrocarril, the fishing dock lined with seafood restaurants, the Museo Tortoni. There is more information here in [this Wikipedia article](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caldera_(Chile)) (in Spanish).

# Caldera, Chile: Taking in the Quiet Fishing Village and Jewel-Colored Bahía Inglesa

[![Image 2: Views from Caldera, Chile](https://farm1.staticflickr.com/701/21258185509_5d9ab1768b_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/21258185509/in/dateposted-public/ "Views from Caldera, Chile")  
_Pelicans and Other Seabirds in Caldera, Chile_

There’s no way around it: northern Chile is vast. Chile is a long, skinny country with miles upon endless miles of coastline, dotted here and there with important port cities or crossroads towns connecting to an inland highway. When heading north from Santiago by land, you may ask yourself one of two questions: can I endure spending 24+ hours on a bus? or, where can I stop?

[![Image 3: Views from Caldera, Chile](https://farm6.staticflickr.com/5633/21434277652_2f1856a100_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/21434277652/in/dateposted-public/ "Views from Caldera, Chile")  
_Quiet Little Beach and Houses Overlooking the Bay of Caldera, Chile_

While I spent 32 hours on a bus [once before](https://www.blueskylimit.com/blog/2013/08/11/six-weeks-on-the-road-in-chile-and-argentina/), I vowed never to do that again. When I decided to visit Iquique for the second half of my winter vacation, I knew I wanted to break the journey somewhere along the way.

[![Image 4: Views from Caldera, Chile](https://farm1.staticflickr.com/614/21434963252_7df95b4d63_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/21434963252/in/dateposted-public/ "Views from Caldera, Chile")  
_Plaza de Armas in Caldera, Chile_

Enter Caldera. Caldera is about 12 hours north of Santiago and 12 hours south of Iquique and located right off the Panamerican highway, making it an easily accessible and convenient stop on a bus journey along the coast. After hearing rave reviews of the town from two of my volunteers, I decided to see it for myself.

[![Image 5: Views from Caldera, Chile](https://farm1.staticflickr.com/564/21433798112_093d394658_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/21433798112/in/dateposted-public/ "Views from Caldera, Chile")  
_Fishing Boats Docked in Caldera, Chile_

Caldera is a town known for its artisanal fishing methods, for being the site of the [first railroad](http://www.memoriachilena.cl/602/w3-article-3401.html) in Chile, for its colonial arquitecture, and for its pleasant beaches. By coincidence, I decided to visit Caldera on the weekend it was celebrating the anniversary of the first railroad, which gave the usually quiet town lots of fun energy and life.

[![Image 6: Views from Caldera, Chile](https://farm6.staticflickr.com/5736/20824291183_0eba350477_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/20824291183/in/dateposted-public/ "Views from Caldera, Chile")  
_Relaxing at the Beach in Caldera, Chile_

To be fair, there isn’t much to do in Caldera except relax. I spent some time sitting by the ocean, looking out at the fishing boats docked in the bay. I took in the colorful plaza, which on one side is your typical Plaza de Armas, and on the other is a mini amusement park. I wandered the streets looking at the colonial buildings. And of course, I ate [artesanal ice cream](https://instagram.com/p/5S0hwauLAf/) from a local shop.

[![Image 7: Views from Caldera, Chile](https://farm6.staticflickr.com/5777/20822515894_e99278b4bf_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/20822515894/in/dateposted-public/ "Views from Caldera, Chile")  
_Converted Train Cars Sell Souvenirs in Caldera, Chile_

I poked around the old railroad station, which is now a Centro Cultural. Because of the anniversary weekend, there were a lot of food stands selling regional treats like my much-loved _churrasca_.

[![Image 8: Churrasca in Caldera, Chile](https://farm6.staticflickr.com/5700/21453207851_46730f03f2_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/21453207851/in/dateposted-public/ "Churrasca in Caldera, Chile")  
_Can’t Resist a Churrasca in Caldera, Chile_

[![Image 9: Views from Caldera, Chile](https://farm6.staticflickr.com/5821/21434206142_d0d870c784_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/21434206142/in/dateposted-public/ "Views from Caldera, Chile")  
_Old Caldera Railway Sign_

After getting a sense of the town, I wandered over to the fishing docks and watched the pelicans, my favorite seabird. I also watched the sea lions lumbering around on the rocks, going about their business.

[![Image 10: Views from Caldera, Chile](https://farm6.staticflickr.com/5808/21434030362_dc15f20e17_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/21434030362/in/dateposted-public/ "Views from Caldera, Chile")  
_Watching the Seabirds Along the Coastal Desert in Caldera, Chile_

[![Image 11: Views from Caldera, Chile](https://farm1.staticflickr.com/717/21257134088_0ff62db9fe_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/21257134088/in/dateposted-public/ "Views from Caldera, Chile")  
_Sea Lion Doing His Thing in Caldera, Chile_

As a vegetarian, I wasn’t tempted by the seafood restaurants or museum on fishing methods, but I did appreciate the murals celebrating traditional fisherman, who also form part of my own family tree, many generations back.

[![Image 12: Views from Caldera, Chile](https://farm1.staticflickr.com/767/21256995268_ef3e5c37c3_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/21256995268/in/dateposted-public/ "Views from Caldera, Chile")  
_Mural of a Traditional Fisherman, Caldera, Chile_

The next morning, the hostal lent me a bike and I headed back into town to watch the main ceremony recreating the first departure of Chile’s first railroad.

[![Image 13: Anniversary of the First Railroad in Chile, Caldera, Chile](https://farm6.staticflickr.com/5648/21444477965_8f042a8369_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/21444477965/in/dateposted-public/ "Anniversary of the First Railroad in Chile, Caldera, Chile")  
_Caldera Residents Dressed in Period Costumes_

I appreciated that so many of Caldera’s residents went all out in wearing traditional clothing from the 1800’s. It was nice to see a celebration that was not religious, but rather historical, in nature. After welcoming trekkers who hiked overnight to arrive in Caldera, it was time to cut the ribbon and board the train.

[![Image 14: Anniversary of the First Railroad in Chile, Caldera, Chile](https://farm6.staticflickr.com/5692/21452883871_f3080a0dfe_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/21452883871/in/dateposted-public/ "Anniversary of the First Railroad in Chile, Caldera, Chile")

[![Image 15: Anniversary of the First Railroad in Chile, Caldera, Chile](https://farm6.staticflickr.com/5710/20821672584_c5881b9516_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/20821672584/in/dateposted-public/ "Anniversary of the First Railroad in Chile, Caldera, Chile")  
_Time to Get on the Train in Caldera, Chile_

From the center of town, I biked over to the other major destination in Caldera, the Gruta del Padre Negro, a small church sanctuary honoring a priest from Colombia who is known for granting miracles.

[![Image 16: Gruta del Padre Negro, Caldera, Chile](https://farm6.staticflickr.com/5823/20821631744_5318ef9f5a_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/20821631744/in/dateposted-public/ "Gruta del Padre Negro, Caldera, Chile")  
_Gruta del Padre Negro, Caldera, Chile_

The small building has colorful murals painted all over its interior and the inviting plaza is also a good place to break for a snack.

[![Image 17: Gruta del Padre Negro, Caldera, Chile](https://farm1.staticflickr.com/681/21256471728_8ec6af155b_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/21256471728/in/dateposted-public/ "Gruta del Padre Negro, Caldera, Chile")

[![Image 18: Gruta del Padre Negro, Caldera, Chile](https://farm1.staticflickr.com/588/20823187353_724f949d78_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/20823187353/in/dateposted-public/ "Gruta del Padre Negro, Caldera, Chile")  
_Murals in the Gruta del Padre Negro, Caldera, Chile_

[![Image 19: Gruta del Padre Negro, Caldera, Chile](https://farm1.staticflickr.com/753/21452737151_36a855e517_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/21452737151/in/dateposted-public/ "Gruta del Padre Negro, Caldera, Chile")  
_Lighting Candles for Miracles in the Gruta del Padre Negro, Caldera, Chile_

I continued along my way the 6km bike path to Bahía Inglesa, a popular tourist destination due to its white sand beaches and jewel-toned waters.

[![Image 20: Views from Bahía Inglesa, Caldera, Chile](https://farm1.staticflickr.com/580/20821433594_2fd1e132fb_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/20821433594/in/dateposted-public/ "Views from Bahía Inglesa, Caldera, Chile")  
_White Sand Beaches and Jewel-Toned Waters in Bahía Inglesa, Caldera, Chile_

[![Image 21: Views from Bahía Inglesa, Caldera, Chile](https://farm1.staticflickr.com/672/21255858840_a3ae4810e9_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/21255858840/in/dateposted-public/ "Views from Bahía Inglesa, Caldera, Chile")  
_Bahía Inglesa, Caldera, Chile_

Bahía Inglesa is even smaller than Caldera, consisting mainly of beachfront restaurants and cabañas for rent during the tourist season. Although I had planned to spend a leisurely afternoon reading on the beach, the winter winds coming off the water were quite chilly so I decided to head back to Caldera.

[![Image 22: Views from Bahía Inglesa, Caldera, Chile](https://farm1.staticflickr.com/782/21255836490_daea3b6b8d_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/21255836490/in/dateposted-public/ "Views from Bahía Inglesa, Caldera, Chile")  
_Selfie with a Photobomb by a Street Dog, Bahía Inglesa, Caldera, Chile_

On the way, I stopped at a viewpoint overlooking Bahía Inglesa, where I took in the surrounding landscape. It surprises me how similar coastal Chile is to coastal Peru, considering the distance, with barren deserts inland and lovely beaches and bays on the water.

[![Image 23: Views from Viewpoint near Bahía Inglesa, Caldera, Chile](https://farm1.staticflickr.com/563/21255746640_9ff4bb4e20_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/21255746640/in/dateposted-public/ "Views from Viewpoint near Bahía Inglesa, Caldera, Chile")  
_Looking Over Bahía Inglesa, Caldera, Chile_

[![Image 24: Views from Viewpoint near Bahía Inglesa, Caldera, Chile](https://farm1.staticflickr.com/573/21255767860_98b12ee210_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/21255767860/in/dateposted-public/ "Views from Viewpoint near Bahía Inglesa, Caldera, Chile")  
_Empty Desert Landscape Near Bahiá Inglesa, Caldera, Chile_

After returning to Caldera, I took another spin around the town. One thing I thought I would love about Caldera is that it hosts a moai from [Easter Island](https://www.blueskylimit.com/blog/category/chile/easter-island-rapa-nui/).

[![Image 25: Moai from Easter Island in Caldera, Chile](https://farm1.staticflickr.com/631/21489411816_d253e163c9_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/21489411816/in/dateposted-public/ "Moai from Easter Island in Caldera, Chile")  
_Moai from Easter Island in Caldera, Chile_

Easter Island is located at about the same latitude as Caldera, so the moai was donated to mark this relationship.

[![Image 26: Moai from Easter Island in Caldera, Chile](https://farm6.staticflickr.com/5723/20894485073_acff23c645_z.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/20894485073/in/dateposted-public/ "Moai from Easter Island in Caldera, Chile")  
_Moai from Easter Island, Looking Out to the Sea in Caldera, Chile_

Unfortunately, as with many moai on mainland Chile, this moai has been treated poorly by visitors and is sadly covered with disgusting graffiti.

[![Image 27: Moai in Caldera, Chile](https://farm1.staticflickr.com/587/21256488880_bba181c8b6_n.jpg)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/blueskylimit/21256488880/in/dateposted-public/ "Moai in Caldera, Chile")  
_Much-Abused But Still Dignified Moai in Caldera, Chile_

As the sun went down, I headed back to my _hostal_ to wait out the remaining hours until my bus to Iquique, where I would spend the remainder of my winter vacation, enjoying the warmer temperatures of the north!

**Recommendations for Caldera, Chile:**

*   Caldera would be a perfect weekend trip and seemed to be a big destination for vacationing couples and families. If I had been in the mood to relax on a retreat, I would have enjoyed staying for longer, but I was antsy to move on to the big city.
*   I stayed at [Hostal El Faro](http://www.casahostalelfaro.com/), which is owned by an extremely sweet woman named Mariela. You can book the hostel through AirBnB or on her [website](http://www.casahostalelfaro.com/). Mariela is incredibly helpful and will pick you up from the bus terminal if you arrange in advance, give you a brief tour of the town to get you situated, and provide suggestions for your visit. She also went out of her way and drove me to the bus station at midnight, and her son lent me a bike for my trip to Bahía Inglesa. I highly recommend staying here as long as you don’t mind being a little ways out of the downtown area. I like walking and it was certainly walkable, but I do suggest using Google Maps to find your way!
*   The Gruta del Padre Negro is located on the outskirts of town and is worth a stop to see some of the religious heritage of the town.
*   As mentioned, I happened to visit when the town was celebrating the anniversary of the first railroad in Chile. I appreciated the period costumes and celebrations for the anniversary of the railroad, and if you’re interested in seeing it for yourself, plan a visit in July. More info [here](http://www.ellapicero.cl/caldera-esta-de-fiesta-por-aniversario-de-primer-ferrocarril/) on the festivities in 2015.
*   Bahia Inglesa is an easy 6km trip on paved bike paths from Caldera, as long as you have a good bike. There are bike rental shops in town, or your hostal may be able to lend you one.
*   There is an artisanal ice cream shop in town, popular among tourists, called Helados Gutierrez.
*   Pullman and Turbus stop at the tiny bus terminal in town, but you want to make sure you book your ticket in advance and store your luggage at your hostal as the offices are not open at all hours.
*   Other sights to see in town are the Centro Cultural Ferrocarril, the fishing dock lined with seafood restaurants, the Museo Tortoni. There is more information here in [this Wikipedia article](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caldera_(Chile)) (in Spanish).

# Beach discovery trip to Caldera, Copiapó – Atacama Chile.

May 24, 2019

Me and my polola decided to go to the region of Atacama for a couple of days. We stayed in a nice, cute house in copiapó. This one is a city in northern Chile! We did some little hikes overthere.

On a very beautiful early morning, we took the car and went to Caldera. This is a nice port city. It has an excellent harbor, used for the productive mining to copiapó and which is connected to the first Chilean railroad.

*   ![Image 3](https://maurititalianinwanderlust.home.blog/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/img_20170102_115325.jpg)

dav

*   ![Image 4](https://maurititalianinwanderlust.home.blog/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/img_20170102_115318.jpg)

dav

After having a great lunch in the famous fishmarket, we went to the ruta del desierto. This is a road in the desert, with a lot of different beautiful beaches. Yup, Anais was missing her ‘beach’ apparently! Island girl!

*   ![Image 5](https://maurititalianinwanderlust.home.blog/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/img_20170103_152331.jpg)

dig

*   ![Image 6](https://maurititalianinwanderlust.home.blog/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/img_20170103_143247.jpg)

dig

We did four of the beaches. First stop was Barranquilla, a very nice one. We had a little romantic beachwalk and decided to go further. Next stop was puerto viejo, famous because of the delicious seafood dishes. Yes! That’s right.. We loved that stop mainly for the food, or at least Anais was the most excited about it, Miss Foodie! We then went to bahia inglesa, which to us was the most pretty one. During the weekends this beach is very popular within the chilenos! We spent a couple of hours over here, to rest a bit, swim and do some snorkeling.

Sunset lovers as we are, we couldn’t end such a beautiful beach day without a perfect sunset and made our way to flamenco beach, where the sunset was just perfectly, romantic-ly breathtaking! With its very beautiful white sand beach, we enjoyed the evening over there, with a delicious dinner at the beach itself!

*   ![Image 7](https://maurititalianinwanderlust.home.blog/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/img_20171229_125652_365.jpg)
*   ![Image 8](https://maurititalianinwanderlust.home.blog/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/img_20170103_153103.jpg)

dav

dav

dav

# Beach discovery trip to Caldera, Copiapó – Atacama Chile.

May 24, 2019

Me and my polola decided to go to the region of Atacama for a couple of days. We stayed in a nice, cute house in copiapó. This one is a city in northern Chile! We did some little hikes overthere.

On a very beautiful early morning, we took the car and went to Caldera. This is a nice port city. It has an excellent harbor, used for the productive mining to copiapó and which is connected to the first Chilean railroad.

*   ![Image 3](https://maurititalianinwanderlust.home.blog/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/img_20170102_115325.jpg)

dav

*   ![Image 4](https://maurititalianinwanderlust.home.blog/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/img_20170102_115318.jpg)

dav

After having a great lunch in the famous fishmarket, we went to the ruta del desierto. This is a road in the desert, with a lot of different beautiful beaches. Yup, Anais was missing her ‘beach’ apparently! Island girl!

*   ![Image 5](https://maurititalianinwanderlust.home.blog/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/img_20170103_152331.jpg)

dig

*   ![Image 6](https://maurititalianinwanderlust.home.blog/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/img_20170103_143247.jpg)

dig

We did four of the beaches. First stop was Barranquilla, a very nice one. We had a little romantic beachwalk and decided to go further. Next stop was puerto viejo, famous because of the delicious seafood dishes. Yes! That’s right.. We loved that stop mainly for the food, or at least Anais was the most excited about it, Miss Foodie! We then went to bahia inglesa, which to us was the most pretty one. During the weekends this beach is very popular within the chilenos! We spent a couple of hours over here, to rest a bit, swim and do some snorkeling.

Sunset lovers as we are, we couldn’t end such a beautiful beach day without a perfect sunset and made our way to flamenco beach, where the sunset was just perfectly, romantic-ly breathtaking! With its very beautiful white sand beach, we enjoyed the evening over there, with a delicious dinner at the beach itself!
